The brief's bundled suite names harness_drive_audio, which exists only after DRIVE-TYPED-2 lands. findings.certainty: READ (mechanism); UNVERIFIED (that libm or CPU differences actually change a profile bit; not measured)
findings.severity: wrong refusal of a valid document on reopen: the whole waveform edit list becomes unusable
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/waveform.rs:641-654 (replay recomputes the print and refuses on any digest difference), :597-616 (noise_print), :771-800 (waveform_sync: a replay error leaves cache None and error set, so selection and edits refuse 'no audio'), :723-731 (source identity already checked); crates/hsk-studio-score/src/denoise.rs:40-47 (FFT twiddles from f64 cos/sin), :95 (sqrt-Hann from cos), :127-138 (digest = SHA-256 over the exact f64 bits of the power spectrum)
findings.what: The stored print_digest pins the exact floating-point output of score's FFT and profiler, whose twiddles and window come from libm cos and sin. On replay, any bit difference refuses waveform_noise_print_stale, and the whole list stops replaying. The two legitimate causes of a stale print are already excluded. The source is identity-checked (waveform_source_mismatch), and the op list is append-only (undo pops the last op), so earlier ops cannot change under a noise op. That leaves only false refusals: (1) another OS or C runtime (MSVC UCRT, glibc and Apple libm differ in the last ulp for some arguments; UCRT also dispatches FMA3 variants of its transcendental functions per CPU); (2) any later change to score's Fft, sqrt_hann or NoiseProfiler (for example a faster FFT); (3) a non-deterministic hosted plugin op earlier in the list. The lane's tests replay on the same machine and build, so they cannot see this.
findings.scenario: An editor saves a package with a noise_reduce op on Windows. A colleague reopens it on macOS, or the same user reopens it after a Studio update that changes the FFT. The replay of op i refuses as stale, waveform_sync sets the cache to None, and every waveform edit in the document, not only the noise op, is unusable until the op is removed by hand.
findings.fix: Lead decision (Q1), since the brief prescribed this check. Preferred: keep print_digest stored, for provenance and the edit report, but do not refuse on mismatch at replay. Or replace the check with a platform-independent one: the prefix_digest of ops[..i] plus the print range, as the clipboard does (waveform.rs prefix_digest). If a digest refusal must stay, compare it only when the op is created, not during replay.

findings.certainty: READ (per-instance and per-list bounds); UNVERIFIED (the bus count Folio's Budget admits; reverb, chorus and click-repair state sizes not summed)
findings.severity: unsafe: no aggregate memory bound (V4-02) when a hostile package opens the mixer
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-score/src/delay.rs:43,:93,:125 (line Vec<f64>, channels*D <= 8Mi samples = 64 MiB per instance); crates/hsk-studio-folio/src/audio_routing.rs:260 (at most 64 effects per list); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/audio_session.rs:605-631 (bus_effect builds each instance); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/mixer.rs:243 (mixer_rebuild), :504/:534/:545 (each edit builds again)
findings.what: Before this lane, a bus or master stack could hold only gain, equalizer, dynamics and the lookahead limiter, all with small state. The table now puts feedback_delay, reverb, chorus, flanger and click_repair on every bus and the master. Each instance is bounded, and each list holds at most 64 instances. Nothing sums the state of all stacks before the graph builds them, and the brief's item 8(e) asked only for per-kind bounds.
findings.scenario: An untrusted package has a master and 8 submix buses, each holding 64 feedback_delay instances with time_ms 5000, and the session runs at 192 kHz. That is 64 x 5 s x 192000 x 2 ch x 8 B = 0.98 GB per list, about 8.8 GB in total, allocated by open_mixer. At 768 kHz each instance is 61 MiB, or 3.9 GB per list. The process aborts on allocation failure instead of refusing typed.
findings.fix: Have each table row estimate its state size before it builds (for example a `state_bytes(params, rate, channels)` beside build_audio_filter: delay line, reverb combs, chorus/flanger lines, click window). Sum it over all stacks in the bus stream build and in bus_effect callers, and refuse typed above a budget (an AudioFilterError or a PulseError::InvalidInput code). Add an aggregate_over_budget test, as V4-02 requires. Or the lead records this as V4-02 debt for the next audio slice (Q4).

findings.severity: round and lane-check exit 73 instead of 0; a proven claim reads NOT_PROVEN
findings.what: The stability test asserts that every pole radius is under 1 at the six rates, which is the brief's stability proof. It then prints a line starting 'NOT_PROVEN:' about the impulse decay that is not run. run-round collects every NOT_PROVEN line in a unit's captured output, and an otherwise green round exits 73, never 0. So the passing stability test is listed as not_proven, and the bundled lane-check over the score suite cannot exit 0.
findings.scenario: Bundled lane-check: every unit passes, the round prints 'NOT_PROVEN hsk-studio-score graphic_eq every_section_is_stable_...' and exits 73. A validator reading round.json not_proven sees the stability AC as not proven.
findings.fix: Keep the radius assertions in this test and print the measurement as 'MEASURED: slowest pole radius ...'. If the lead wants the decay listed, move the NOT_PROVEN line into its own test, for example `impulse_decay_below_1e6_not_run`, so only that claim is NOT_PROVEN.
